intent_en: To demonstrate that income inequality in the United States has returned to levels seen during the Great Depression.
previous_intent: To illustrate the historical trend of income inequality in the United States, demonstrating that the share of national income held by the top earners has returned to levels comparable to the Great Depression.
narration_support: income inequality is at its highest level since the Great Depression.
chart_support: Line chart showing the share of national income for the top 10% in the US from 1910 to 2010, displaying a U-shaped trend with peaks around 1930 and 2010.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly claims income inequality is at its highest since the Great Depression. The chart visualizes this by plotting the 'Share of top percentage in national income' (Top 10%) from 1910-2010, showing values around 50% in the late 1920s and again in 2010, supporting the claim of a return to historical highs.
